set.reason: The Daoist appellation 'Zi Qing' (Reverend/Perfected Zi Qing) was localized to 'Augustus' with the title 'Zhenren/Reverend' rendered as 'Saint'. Corrected during reconciliation: the earlier claim of 'tianqiong' belongs to Saint Viana (Zhenren Tianqiong).
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: batch_16 claimed source 'tianqiong', which is Saint Viana's counterpart; Saint Augustus = Zi Qing.

set.reason: The entitled young heir of House Moon was localized as 'Yates Moon'; his source counterpart is Mo Yu, the arrogant young relative who taunts Mo Can (Ethan) at the family gathering. His father Mo Xiuyan = James Moon.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'mo xiuyan', which is his father James Moon; Yates is the son, Mo Yu.
Human alias 'Josh' (Eps 436, 447, 980) is the same entity (the dragon's unassuming human persona); the 'Josh' row was merged into this one during reconciliation.

Surname collision: this Elder Shaw (leader of the Sea Wyrm Sect, Eps 687-773, = source Sect Master Xiao) is a different character from Liam Shaw and Yolande Shaw (Eps 58-145). Do not merge the three under one entity. The standalone 'Shaw' row was merged into this one during reconciliation.

Name collision: the Ep 336 mention 'House Carter' (one of the five Castermere County families) is a separate entity sharing the surname, folded into the merged 'Carter' row's mentions. The standalone 'Carter' row was merged into this one during reconciliation.

NAME COLLISION: 'Julian' in Eps 56-61 is Julian Croft, the early Skyreach antagonist who lent the Indigo Blade - a completely different character from this Elder Julian of Eps 439-450 (Dragonblaze Hall recruiter, = source Zhao Zheng). Do not merge their mentions. The standalone 'Julian' row was merged into this one during reconciliation.

Two different characters share the name 'Howard': a Stormcrown Peak apprentice ranked near Felix and Preston Sterling (Ep 118), and this Elder Howard (= source Elder Wei) who brings Zane to the Baptism by Laws (Eps 438-449). The Ep 118 mentions must not be merged into this entity. The standalone 'Howard' row was merged into this one during reconciliation.

set.reason: The source's Heaven's Might Demon King - the second famous Demon King attacking White Emperor City alongside the Black Iron Demon King (chs 118-131), fought head-on by the hammer-wielding Xing Tiansu (= Axel) - was given the personal name 'Orion' and the title 'Dreadlord'.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'black iron demon king', which is Aldrich (the Dreadlord tied to the Hellfire and the Life Force duel). Orion is the other famous Demon King of the same battle, Heaven's Might Demon King, fought by Axel/Xing Tiansu with his massive hammers (ch 120 vs Ep 136).

set.reason: The enemy swordsman of the Illusion Battlefield's Third Karma Hall, Dugu Jian Xiaoxiao - famous for humbling a prodigy of the Ten Thousand Buddha Sacred Domain and carrying a sentient dark-iron sword - was localized as 'Larkin'.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'jin hai', but Jin Hai fights on Zane's side (rendered as Jeffrey/Coleman). Larkin's scenes match Dugu Jian Xiaoxiao exactly: the sentient old sword smuggled into the Battlefield, the hook tug-of-war with Zane over the energy river, 'Damon, ignore them' spoken beside Damon/Big Dream, and Janet recognizing him as the warrior 'infamous across the Hallowed Concord for humbling one of its own prodigies' (chs 1265-1272). batch_46's 'Otherworldly Swordsman' row already aliases to Larkin with this source name.
set.description: The enemy swordsman of the Karma Hall standoff (Eps 1276-1286): a warrior made famous by a single battle in which he humbled a prodigy of the Hallowed Concord. He smuggled his sentient dark-iron sword into the Illusion Battlefield and fights Zane in a hook tug-of-war over the river of energy, falling in and surviving its corrosion thanks to the weakened blade (source: Dugu Jian Xiaoxiao, chs 1265-1272).

set.issues: Distinct from the MasterLS entry 'Jeff' (Ep 247, ranked 99th in Skyreach Sect Rankings) - that is a different minor character; this Jeffrey appears only in Eps 1273-1315. SPLIT: same source character 'Jin Hai' as Coleman (both Eps 1273-1318). Jeffrey carries Jin Hai's monk persona ('the famous monk from The Hallowed Concord'), his conjured fog ('someone over there can see through my fog'), the Dark Law identification and the borrowed Buddha Sun Blade (Blade of Hallowed Censure, incl. the distance-gauging scene, ch 1288); Coleman carries Jin Hai's hook feats and the killing of Damon/Big Dream.

SPLIT: same source character 'Jin Hai' as Jeffrey (both Eps 1273-1318). Coleman carries Jin Hai's hook feats - first to smash his tablet and pull his hook free, hooking Damon the instant his Forceful Crystal Armor forms, and sweeping the Blade of Hallowed Censure across Damon's throat (= Jin Hai vs Big Dream, chs 1266-1267) - while Jeffrey carries the monk persona, the fog and the blade's ownership.

set.reason: Zane's early sect friend of humble origins was localized as 'Rhys Bolton'; his source counterpart is Zhou Xian, one of the two young disciples (with Mo Can) who befriend Luo Zheng from the entry trials onward.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'zhang wuxian', who is Dustin Blackwood (the House Blackwood/Zhang Clan merchant scion). Rhys's episode range (Eps 52-208) maps exactly onto Zhou Xian's chapters (chs 37-195), and his 'humble origins with no noteworthy connections' profile matches Zhou Xian, not the Zhang Clan heir.

set.reason: The stocky, hot-tempered disciple of the Razorwing frontier campaign was localized as 'Max'; his source counterpart is Zhao Xuyong, one of the four Blue Cloud Sect disciples (with Luo Zheng, Yang Tai and Meng Changjun/Leo) who stay to hunt blade insects with the Imperial Army at Dragon Castle.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'zhang wuxian' (= Dustin Blackwood). The fort trio Max/Rex/Leo (Eps 64-75) maps to Zhao Xuyong/Yang Tai/Meng Changjun (chs 49-60); Zhang Wuxian does not appear in those chapters. NAME COLLISION: the dossier also folds in an unrelated later 'Max' of the Demi-Immortal Race group around the Tower of Sin (Eps 912-969, with Dorothea and Delroy) - a different character; the Ep 969 'reunion' line is about that Max, not a Fatty Zhang reunion.
set.description: A stocky, hot-tempered Skyreach Sect disciple and one of Zane's earliest battle companions, part of the circle with Leo and the ill-fated Rex from the Razorwing campaign at the frontier fort (Eps 64-75; source: Zhao Xuyong, chs 49-60). Note: the later 'Max' of Eps 912-969, who travels with the Demi-Immortal Race group to the Tower of Sin, is a different character folded into this surface form.

set.reason: Max's close friend, the sharp-eyed disciplined disciple killed in the Razorwing campaign, was localized as 'Rex'; his source counterpart is Yang Tai, cut in two by the Blade Insect Queen (ch ~58).
set.issues: Source match assigned during reconciliation: the fort four (Zane/Max/Rex/Leo, Eps 64-75) are Luo Zheng/Zhao Xuyong/Yang Tai/Meng Changjun (chs 49-60); Leo = Meng Changjun was already matched, and the ill-fated member who dies to the Blade Insect Queen is Yang Tai.

SPLIT: same source character 'Zhan Yun' as Gregory, Eps 800-805 vs Eps 788-798. Edwin renders Zhan Yun's duel against Logan/Yun Longtao with the saber Dragon's Tooth ('forged from the teeth of a true dragon... a martial artist who only knows how to retreat will eventually be defeated', verbatim from ch 779), while Gregory renders Zhan Yun's Crystal/Jade Martial House assessment scenes. The show pairs Edwin and Gregory as the Crown Prince's two champions where the source pairs Zhan Yun with Xiao Daoyuan.

SPLIT: same source character 'Zhan Yun' as Edwin, Eps 788-798 vs Eps 800-805. Gregory renders Zhan Yun at the Crystal Martial House assessment (his heart hammering as he measures Zane, ch 767) and as the one who reports the examination to the Crown Prince, while Edwin renders Zhan Yun's Dragon's Tooth duel against Logan/Yun Longtao (ch 779).

set.reason: The Wisteria Martial House legend defeated before the emperors was localized as 'Titus'; his source counterpart is Zhao Tianji, the Fire Law prodigy whose ferocious attacks cannot break Yun Longtao's Space Armor (chs 777-778).
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'zhan yun' (= Edwin/Gregory). Titus's fight is verbatim Zhao Tianji's: mastery of the Law of Fire, attacks 'fierce - probably the strongest of any Spirit-Tribulation warrior there', smothered by Logan/Yun Longtao's Spatial Armor, and defeated (Eps 800-801 vs chs 777-778).

set.reason: The Demon Night girl who attends her clan's Queen and guides Zane through the Tower of Sin was localized as 'Phoebe' (echoing the source name Fei'er).
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'xia shuang', who is human (Purple Heart Holy Land genius = Olivia). Phoebe's scenes are Fei'er's: assigned to stick to Luo Zheng until Lord Mei arrives, explaining the Tower's floors on the way up, the calm apologetic smiles (chs 550-563), and the Yao Ye Clan's Cursed Land explanation in the later arc (Eps 565-578, 666).

set.reason: The Demon Night's seat holder in the Tower of Sin was localized as 'Madeline'; her source counterpart is Bai Huan, controller of the Yao Ye Clan's seats.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'xia shuang', who is the human Tower-circle girl (= Olivia). Madeline's profile is verbatim Bai Huan's: 'only a tenth rank warrior, but her soul has already reached the Battle Soul Realm', and onlookers burned for looking at her with lustful thoughts (ch 583 vs Ep 598).
set.description: The Demon Night's seat holder in the Tower of Sin (Eps 598-608), reputedly only a tenth-level War Lord but with a soul already at the Fighting Soul Realm; onlookers say anyone who eyes her with impure thoughts gets burned. She studies the wall of names where Zane, a mere human War Fighter, has claimed a first-row spot (source: Bai Huan, controller of the Yao Ye Clan, chs 583-595).

set.issues: SPLIT: same source character 'Lan Bing' as Chantel, Eps 943-949 vs Eps 945-948 (chs 920-926). Lacey carries Lan Bing's barrier fighting and her signature tongue-biting essence-blood bursts (ch 922: 'she gently bit the tip of her tongue... and burned her essence blood'); Chantel carries Lan Bing's intervention against the Demon Race patriarch Mo Xiao ('Your opponent is me!', ch 920).

Affiliation inconsistency: Ep 945 calls Chantel 'one of the Heavenly Feather Sanctuary's own masters' while Ep 946 calls her 'one of the Demon Night's Soul Sea Realm masters'; in the source Lady Lan Bing is a Divine Sea Realm expert of the Demon Night Clan's Heavenly Feather Holy Land, so both are true (ch 920). SPLIT: same source character 'Lan Bing' as Lacey, Eps 945-948 vs Eps 943-949 (chs 920-926). Chantel carries Lan Bing's intervention against Mo Xiao ('Your opponent is me!'); Lacey carries her tongue-biting essence-blood bursts and barrier fighting.

set.reason: The gruff, extortionately priced healer who saves Zane's life was localized as 'Payne'; his source counterpart is Xue Taiping, the greedy miracle-working doctor of White Emperor City.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'zhu feihang', who is Lennie (the military doctor, Ingrid's uncle, who stabilizes Zane with the golden needle). Payne's role is Xue Taiping's: the famously greedy miracle doctor whose 'price is extremely high', hired to treat Luo Zheng's destroyed organs (chs 108-110 vs Eps 122-123).
set.description: A gruff healer at The Crucible (Eps 122-123) notorious for quoting astronomical prices - he once let a man bleed out over his fee. He nonetheless spends six grueling hours saving Zane's life, emerging drenched in sweat to a waiting Ingrid, and is intrigued by the strangeness of Zane's wounds (source: Xue Taiping, the greedy miracle-working doctor of White Emperor City, chs 108-110).

set.issues: Name drift: the master sheet lists him as 'Cecil Moreau', but the delivered Ep 249 announces him as 'Cecil Sterling' and Ep 250 references House Sterling - 'Sterling' is canonical. Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'zhou dan', who is Richard (the Blackrock/Hei Peak top disciple with the weasel-hair writing brush and Thirteen Kills, chs 240-247). Cecil's fight is Zhuge Xi's: the House Sterling (Zhuge Family) fighter whose feather fan bears a living, slowly rotating eight-trigrams cipher and whips up wind cyclones (chs 234-236 vs Eps 249-253).
set.reason: The fan-wielding House Sterling fighter of the arena competition was localized as 'Cecil Sterling'; his source counterpart is Zhuge Xi of the Zhuge Family, whose Yin and Yang Fan carries a rotating eight-trigrams pattern.
set.description: A Soul Realm fighter of House Sterling who faces Zane in the arena competition (Eps 249-264), announced by Master Young with evident relish. He fights with a fan etched with an intricate, living Runic Cipher (source: Zhuge Xi's Yin and Yang Fan with its slowly rotating eight trigrams), whipping up cyclones with cunning, predatory patience. He came to the arena with motives beyond the fight itself (Ep 249).

set.issues: SPLIT: same source character 'Che Daozi' as Barrett, Eps 154-293 vs Eps 98-143. The source's single dead Master Artificer left both relics: the auctioned secret journal (rendered as Barrett's 'Principles of Forging', chs 84-95) and the unfinished sword he died refining plus his cipher writings (rendered as Chase's legacy: 'he never woke up again', ch 139-143). The show renamed the same dead weaponsmith between arcs.

SPLIT: same source character 'Che Daozi' as Chase, Eps 98-143 vs Eps 154-293. Barrett carries the auctioned journal (Principles of Forging = Che Daozi's Weapon Refining Ancestral Techniques, chs 84-95); Chase carries the unfinished dying-breath blade and the book of ciphers (chs 139-143).

set.reason: The third of the brothers exploring the underground palace was localized as 'Cody'; his source counterpart is Hou San, the loud complainer whom Hou Da (= Abner) sends into the darkness.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'hou da', who is Abner - in Ep 1134 it is Abner who leads the brothers and orders 'Cody. Go take a look', matching Hou Da sending Hou San into the darkness (ch 1114). Cody also matches Hou San's presence in the Abyss of Samsara chapter (Ep 1152 vs ch 1133).
set.description: The third of the band of brothers exploring the underground depths with a Lantern Pearl (source: Hou San of the seven Hou brothers in the Yin Luo Underground Palace), the loudest complainer on the walk in, sent ahead into the darkness by his eldest brother (Abner/Hou Da) and attacked by the Black Eating Moths (Ep 1134). In Ep 1152 he slides off the icy platform and vanishes into the third level of the Endless Abyss.

set.reason: The lode extortionist slapped flying by Zane was given the Western name 'Ernest'; his source counterpart, the bald self-styled 'Lord of the Southern Sky Kingdom' (a Qiu Ren subordinate), is never named.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'qiu ren', but Qiu Ren is the careful mine boss who sends his crew to make Zane disappear (= Rylan, Eps 1020-1026 / chs 997-1003). Ernest renders Qiu Ren's unnamed bald subordinate, the lode extortionist whom Luo Zheng slaps into the lode (chs ~991-998); some of boss Qiu Ren's extortion-racket framing is folded into Ernest's Ep 1015 offer.
set.description: A bully who controls a mining lode and extorts newcomers (Eps 1014-1021), offering Zane the choice to hand over every Sovereign Stone and deliver more daily, or die. Zane answers by sending him flying with a single slap, and Ernest's crew spreads the tale (source: the unnamed bald cultivator, a subordinate of the lode boss Qiu Ren/Rylan, chs ~991-998).

set.issues: SPLIT: same source character 'Xie Yun' as Shayna. The single source duel Xie Yun vs Pei Tianyao (Patrick, chs 264-267) is rendered with Shayna fighting Patrick in Ep 280 and Wynn fighting Patrick in Ep 281, both wielding the heavy machete and the Reaper's Chop; the two also co-appear on screen as distinct Skytop disciples ('Wynn and Shayna stood silently', Ep 258).

Gender mismatch: episodes consistently portray Shayna as female ('her machete', 'she channeled her Vitality', Ep 280), but the matched source character Xie Yun (the Three Layered Waves saber user who fights Pei Tianyao/Patrick in ch 267) is male (m11/f0). SPLIT: same source character 'Xie Yun' as Wynn - the same duel against Patrick continues as Shayna in Ep 280 and as Wynn in Ep 281, both with the Reaper's Chop machete, and the two co-appear as distinct Skytop disciples in Ep 258.

set.reason: The Groundstone Hall fighter who demands Zane's sword and is sent flying by a single punch was localized as 'Jared Bishop'; his source counterpart is Bi Yuanjia, who demands the Thunder Wind Ghost Sword and is punched flying by Luo Zheng.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'xie mang' (= Ryder, the Divine Weapon Hall sword-trial competitor, Eps 1045-1052 / chs 1022-1029). Jared's scene is Bi Yuanjia's: 'I'm Jared Bishop, ranked fourth in Groundstone Hall' demanding the sword, then sent flying like a deflated ball by one punch (Ep 1056-1057 vs ch 1033). Not to be merged with Bishop Sterling (see the 'Bishop' row's collision note).

set.reason: The second of the two leading human seat holders in the Tower of Sin was localized as 'Jarrod'; his source counterpart is Zhou Zhuohe, Zhao Fenqin's constant companion.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'zhao fenqin', who is Fabian. Decisive line: source Meng Chong sneers 'Zhao Fenqin? ... Where's Zhou Zhuohe? Don't the two of you always appear together?' (ch 582), rendered as Malcolm's 'Fabian. Where's Jarrod? The two of you are usually joined at the hip' (Ep 597). The Book of Celestial Rank exchange likewise maps Fabian to Fenqin (the one addressed) and Jarrod to Zhou Zhuohe.

set.reason: The Tower of Sin's strongest seat holder in lava-lined red armor was localized as 'Maurice'; his source counterpart is Meng Tian, the second seat of the 128.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'meng chong', who is Malcolm (the Ogre/Devil-Race seat holder who declares the death sentence on Zane). Maurice's profile is verbatim Meng Tian's: 'the second seat controller out of the 128 seats... the strongest person in the Sin Tower', fiery red armor with lava-like glowing lines and volcanic heat (ch 591 vs Ep 609).

SPLIT: same source character 'Luo Junyi' (Zane's third uncle) as Ken Lowell, Eps 13-89 vs Eps 326-335. Owen renders Luo Junyi's early House Lowell arc - presiding over family affairs and announcing Perrin's (Luo Peiran's) sect acceptance from the high platform (ch 7) and serving as the accomplice manipulated in the murder of Zane's father; Ken renders Luo Junyi's later arc as Andrew's (Luo Chengyun's) father with the Blood Prisoner pact (chs 313-322).

SPLIT: same source character 'Luo Junyi' (Zane's third uncle) as Owen Lowell, Eps 326-335 vs Eps 13-89. Ken renders Luo Junyi's later arc as the father of Andrew/Luo Chengyun during the House Lowell reckoning (chs 313-322; in the source it is Luo Junyi himself who holds the secret flesh-and-blood pact with the Blood Prisoner, ch ~317); Owen renders Luo Junyi's early-arc deeds (announcing Perrin's acceptance, ch 7).

set.reason: Zane's oldest uncle, the true architect of his father's murder, was localized as 'Nolan'; his source counterpart is Luo Bingquan, the second uncle and mastermind who confronts Luo Zheng with levitated purple swords.
set.issues: Surname collision merges two characters: 'Nolan' (Zane's uncle Nolan Lowell, Eps 8-21) and 'Alan Nolan' (vice leader of the Dragonblaze Hall, Eps 447-448, verified in episode text). The Ep 447-448 mentions belong to the separate character Alan Nolan, not the uncle. Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'luo junyi' (= Owen/Ken Lowell). Nolan's flying-sword confrontation ('I let you live... Since you're so eager to die, I'll be happy to grant your wish', Ep 18) is verbatim Luo Bingquan's (ch 8), and the show names Nolan the mastermind who manipulated his younger brother Owen - matching Luo Bingquan (mastermind) and Luo Junyi (accomplice). SPLIT: same source character 'Luo Bingquan' as Bryson Lowell (Eps 8-21 vs Eps 326-335).

SPLIT: same source character 'Luo Bingquan' as Nolan - Nolan renders Luo Bingquan's early flying-sword confrontation with Zane (Eps 8-21 / ch 8), Bryson Lowell the later House Lowell reckoning arc (Eps 326-335 / chs 313-322).

set.reason: The Lord of House Hawthorne, Darcy's father, was localized as 'Chuck'; his source counterpart is Huang Chen, head of the Huang Family and Huang Xing's father.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'luo junyi' (= Owen/Ken Lowell). Chuck is Darcy's father, and Darcy = Huang Xing (batch_17); source Huang Chen is 'the head of the Huang Family... also Huang Xing's father', the strongest family head in the county at Xiantian fifth stage who found a great opportunity to break through three levels in a row (ch 315/320 vs Eps 327-337).
set.description: Lord of House Hawthorne and Darcy's father, reputedly the most powerful man in Castermere County at the fifth level of the Adept Realm; he somehow found the resources to let Darcy jump three power levels in a row (Eps 327-330). After Zane kills Darcy, Zane cuts off Chuck's right hand along with Ford's in Ep 336, leaving the two most respected fighters in the county on their knees, and Chuck is forced to compensate House Lowell (source: Huang Chen, head of the Huang Family, chs 315-324).

set.reason: The Vanguard One Hundred fighter hired to challenge Zane at the Myriad Spirit House was localized as 'Mervin Thorne'; his source counterpart is Tie Feiyu, the top-100 genius the resentful young cultivators pay to fight Luo Zheng.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'sima yulong', who is Fenton (the Soulbound Sect's number one genius, batch_46 'Fenton Summers'). Mervin's scene is Tie Feiyu's: 'I'll go look for him! I think Tie Feiyu is not bad' becomes 'I'll go get him! Mervin Thorne would be perfect', the hired top-100 challenger enraged at being told he isn't qualified (chs 1008-1010 vs Eps 1031-1037).
set.description: A hired challenger in the Myriad Spirit House arc (Eps 1031-1037): a ruthless-looking fighter of the Vanguard One Hundred with three blood-colored scars, brought in by resentful local talents to put the Lower World ascender in his place, and enraged when Zane tells him he isn't qualified (source: Tie Feiyu, the top-100 genius of the Spirit Martial Holy Land, chs 1008-1010).

set.reason: The Varsity swordsman with Twin Blades who duels a demon general was localized as 'Dalton'; his source counterpart is Zhu Tianlai, the Lone Sky Summit inner disciple who faces a Demon General head-on with paired black-and-white swords.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: the row claimed 'lin geng', who is Cliff (the Misty Peak Varsity leader with the demon-slaying boast, ch 97). Dalton's scene is Zhu Tianlai's: the twin-blade fighter whose demon-general opponent freezes mid-swing to stare at Zane (Ep 116 vs ch 102, 'the Demon General who was fighting fiercely with Zhu Tianlai had obviously slowed down... staring at Luo Zheng').

SPLIT: same source character 'Mie' as Exterminator. Cassian renders Mie as the Queen's devoted spear-wielder (the only man among the four who followed Xun/Lavender, who nearly died protecting her exploring the Abyss of Reincarnation and whose eyes soften when he sees her, chs 1141-1148 vs Eps 1161-1170); the show then kills Cassian off and renders Mie's later scenes as the separately-dispatched 'Exterminator' (Eps 1171-1174). 'Exterminator' is a literal translation of the source name Mie.

SPLIT: same source character 'Mie' as Cassian. In Ep 1171 the Queen of Punishment says the four loyalists (incl. Cassian) died, then dispatches 'the Exterminator' - but in the source it is the same Mie whom Yao sends to the Sifting Yin World (ch 1141) and who confronts Xun at the Wheel of Reincarnation (chs 1148-1152). 'Exterminator' is the literal translation of 'Mie'; the show renders one source character as two entities.

set.reason: The leader of the second-largest human faction of the upper world was localized as 'Lumen'; his source counterpart is Empyrean Oracle, who leads 3,000 great realms against Empyrean Original Sin's 4,000.
set.issues: Source match reassigned during reconciliation: batch_40 had tentatively claimed 'empyrean original sin', but that is Malachi (leader of the largest faction, 4,000 realms); Lumen's three thousand realms match Empyrean Oracle exactly (ch 652 vs Ep 671), as batch_45 found.

Master sheet calls him 'Sterling family leader' but Ep 58 establishes him as the third son of House Sterling; episodes are authoritative. SPLIT: same source character 'Zhuge Feng' (the Zhuge Family's 'Crazy Three', i.e. third young master) as Frey - Felix carries Zhuge Feng's early House Sterling schemes against Zane (Eps 58-118 / chs 43-104), Frey his Sevenfold Phantom Blade ambush (Eps 169-176 / chs 154-162). Ep 99's 'Bishop Sterling' name-drop is a third rendering of the same source figure (see the 'Bishop' row).

SPLIT: same source character 'Zhuge Feng' as Felix Sterling, Eps 169-176 vs Eps 58-118. Frey's ambush is verbatim Zhuge Feng's: a scion of House Sterling attacking with Vivian, summoning the Sevenfold Phantom Blade - orange-red giant swords each held by an invisible swordsman (= the Zhuge Family's 'Seven Mysterious Demonic Sword', chs 156-158).

Merged surface form: 'Bishop' refers to at least three distinct characters across episode ranges - Bishop Sterling (Ep 99, Paige's master, = source Zhuge Feng), Jared Bishop (Ep 1056, a different fighter, = source Bi Yuanjia), and Alice Bishop (Ep 478, the innkeeper's daughter). The Ep 1056 and Ep 478 mentions must not be counted under Bishop Sterling. Note: Bishop Sterling's Ep 99 mention is a third rendering of Zhuge Feng alongside Felix Sterling (Eps 58-118) and Frey (Eps 169-176); see the SPLIT notes on those rows.

set.reason: Minor character given a Western name.
set.description: One of two Ogre War Sages, alongside Colin, in the Tower of Sin arc (Eps 612-613). The pair shoot toward the Tower of Sin's doors like living cannonballs, flatly demanding Zane's death ('The only negotiation is that the boy dies', Ep 613).

set.issues: Name drift: 'Sacred Weapon' used in ~19 episodes vs canonical tier-4 name 'Sacred Arms' (Ep 70 standard).
set.reason: Tier-4 class of the five-tier magical weapon ladder (Mysterious Weapon, Spirit Weapon, Mythic Weapon, Sacred Arms, Divine Arms).
set.description: The fourth tier of magical weapons in the show's weapon grading system, above Mythic Weapon and below Divine Arms. Canonical name per the Ep 70 standard is 'Sacred Arms'; 'Sacred Weapon' is a recurring drift variant.

set.reason: Stanley's technique via the Gold Flower Fan; named for its razor-thin golden threads.
set.description: A combat technique used by Stanley via the Gold Flower Fan (Spirit Weapon): projects a net of razor-thin golden threads. Source counterpart is Pu Xingyu's golden-thread net (chs 250-251).

set.reason: Cooperative formation weapon of Cloud Hall, powered by the Formation of the Twelve Signs.
set.description: A cooperative formation weapon wielded by Lennon Anderson's thirteen Cloud Hall disciples on the Cloud Road, powered by the Formation of the Twelve Signs (source: twelve earthly branches formation).

set.reason: Sword technique renamed for the Western fantasy register.
set.description: A flowering sword technique whose strikes scatter into countless petal-like blade images; localizes the source's 'vibrant falling petals sword'.

set.reason: Minor prodigy given a full Western name.
set.description: A prodigy of Cloudswallow Hall encountered during the Upper World halls arc.

set.reason: The ancient Dragon-blooded clan leader's Chinese name (Feng Xiao) was fully localized to a Western name; the surname 'Shaw' follows the adaptation's naming conventions.
The source's 'Demon Race' was renamed 'Ogres' to give the antagonist race a distinct Western fantasy identity and avoid collision with the show's other demon terminology.
The source term 'Monster Core' was localized as 'Demon Core' to match the show's demon-race terminology.
The source rank/title 'War Emperor' was rendered 'War King' in parts of the adaptation; a Western-register title for the same tier.
